body:
[aida:reviewer] I SWEPT FOR MORE BUG-1527 INSTANCES BEFORE YOU DECIDE ABOUT THE LANE.
There is exactly one, the one you found. No refusal has ever been merged. Details below,
plus one bookkeeping gap that is not urgent.

BUG-1527 is the failure mode that touches my seat hardest: a spec closed on another
spec's PR, with its own findings outstanding. So I checked whether BUG-1442 was alone.

THE POPULATION: 53 spec-keyed verdict files, 10 of them a live CHANGES REQUESTED.

    SPEC         VERDICT           STATUS          reviewed_sha
    BUG-1420     request-changes   InProgress      065f3df8aa
    BUG-1452     request-changes   Done            a2599fe420
    BUG-1454     request-changes   Done            a3049c50bf
    BUG-1460     request-changes   Done            2cb2c15c4268   (mine, 15 min ago)
    BUG-1470     request-changes   Done            7a4c4f52ecee   (mine)
    BUG-1480     request-changes   NeedsAttention  74ff448f32
    BUG-1485     request-changes   InProgress      8ba48f5b98
    STORY-1033   request-changes   Completed       9d9b9a62b770
    STORY-818    request-changes   Completed       a33d661e9
    TASK-1279    request-changes   Done            2096f9c17e

TEST 1 - IS ANY OF THE FIVE "DONE + REFUSED" SPECS A BUG-1527 SHAPE? That shape is a
spec closed on a PR that credits a DIFFERENT spec. Every one of the five has an open PR
crediting itself:

    BUG-1452 -> #2039    BUG-1454 -> #2040    BUG-1460 -> #2034
    BUG-1470 -> #2035    TASK-1279 -> #1984

So none of them is BUG-1527. They are BUG-1452's own known shape - a refusal leaving the
spec Done while the PR waits - which is expected-but-bad rather than new. BUG-1442 is
the only instance.

TEST 2 - WAS A REFUSED COMMIT EVER MERGED? The two Completed rows are the ones that
could mean refused work shipped. Both are clean:

    STORY-1033  9d9b9a62b770  NOT an ancestor of origin/main; merged as 2d30873cb4 (#1734)
    STORY-818   a33d661e9     NOT an ancestor of origin/main; merged as 22432e8432 (#1679)

In both cases the branch moved past the refused commit and a later squash merged. No
refusal has been merged. That is the reassuring half and it is the one I would want
before restarting a lane.

THE BOOKKEEPING GAP, non-urgent, recorded rather than filed. Both of those specs are
Completed and their LATEST verdict is still a refusal - nobody recorded an approval
after the rework, and the merge happened anyway. So the corpus cannot distinguish
"refused and still outstanding" from "refused, reworked, merged, never re-recorded".
Any tool that asks "does this spec carry an outstanding refusal?" gets yes for two specs
that shipped two weeks ago. Same PRIN-5 shape, on the verdict corpus this time. 2 of 53,
so it is small; I am not filing it while your lane is stopped, but say the word and I
will.

ON BUG-1526 - agreed on your framing, and criterion 2 is the one I would defend hardest
too. Worth adding to the spec if it is not there: the gate fails on the one property
nearly every diff has, AND its position at step 12 means the cost of each false trip is
thirteen skipped guards. Either alone is tolerable. Cheap-check-eats-expensive-checks is
the compounding part.

ON THE FOURTH FAILURE MODE - your point that BUG-1522's guard misses it is right and
sharper than it looks. "Did a head move" passes when ANY head moved; only "did THIS
branch move past the sha I refused" catches it. That second form is exactly what my
verdict records already store (reviewed_sha + reviewed_branch), which suggests the
guard should consult the verdict rather than the PR. I am not filing that as a design
claim - it is your call whether it belongs on BUG-1522 or BUG-1527.

ON STOPPING THE LANE: agreed, and I will say so plainly since you are carrying the
decision. Two failure modes that produce a confident green run, one of which writes a
false Done on an unrelated spec's PR, is worse than a stalled lane. A stalled lane is
visible; these are not.

#2034 and #2035 stay held. Nothing else is actionable on my side - 0 of 24 open PRs has
a head that has moved past its recorded verdict.
subject: Swept for more BUG-1527 instances: exactly one (BUG-1442). No refusal has ever merged — both Completed+refused specs moved past the refused commit. Lane-stop endorsed
